name: sages-resume
description: Session start: surface in-progress DAGs from .pi/orchestrator so the user knows what to pick up. Quiet unless something is in flight.
prompt:
Sages session resume. The previous session may have left in-progress DAGs in `.pi/orchestrator/`. Surface them so the user can pick up where they left off. Quiet unless there's actually work to resume.

Steps:

1. Read `.pi/orchestrator/goal-*.yaml` and `.pi/orchestrator/dag-*.yaml` directly with the `read` tool. (Do not run find/ls via bash — these paths are well-known.)

2. For each goal, check the matching DAG. If the DAG has any tasks in `in_progress` or `failed` status, the goal is "active".

3. If no active goals exist, output `[~]` and exit. This is the most common case and should be silent.

4. If active goals exist, build a session-resume summary:
   - For each active goal, one line: `GC-{id} '{title}' — {completed}/{total} done, blocked on: {task_ids}`
   - Plus a recommended next action: `Pick one to resume, or close out blockers before starting new work.`

5. Output the summary as a regular user message in the conversation (it will appear in the transcript and the user sees it on session start). Format:
   ```
   [↻ resuming previous work]
   - GC-2026-XXX 'title' — 2/4 done, blocked on: T3
   - GC-2026-YYY 'title' — 0/3 done, blocked on: T1, T2
   Pick one to resume, or close out blockers before starting new work.
   ```

6. For each active goal, also call `sages_reminder({ type: "RESUME_REQUIRED", dag_id: "GC-{id}" })` so the reminder surfaces in the LLM context for the rest of the session. This makes the in-progress state sticky across turns.

7. If even one `sages_reminder` call hits an error, do NOT abort — log the error text in the session message and continue. The summary is the primary deliverable; the reminder is best-effort.

8. Do NOT call `dag_synthesize`, `task_dispatch`, or any orchestrator tool that mutates state. This routine is observation-only — it surfaces, it does not act.

Reference: `pi/src/tools/orchestrator/sages-reminder.ts` (GC-2026-053). The `RESUME_REQUIRED` reminder type is part of the Sages reminder taxonomy.
